newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam redraws its internal map.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam redraws its internal map.

text.p: Vietnam is to redraw a map of its internal boundaries, creating 61 cities and provinces in total, just two short of the administrative chart under French colonial rule.
State media reported on Thursday that the National Assembly had agreed to the move in order to strengthen provincial management.
However, a number of assembly delegates were reported to have opposed the measure. A decision to separate the ancient capital of Hue from its surrounding province was dropped.
Under a complicated system of remapping, eight existing provinces will be divided into 15 provinces and one city.
For the first time Da Nang, on the central coast, will have the administrative status of a city. But most of the divided provinces surround the capital city, Hanoi.
Vietnam's population is around 75 million. It has had 53 provinces and cities since 1991.
